US-119-HR10882.title: Veteran Breast Cancer Fairness Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10882.description: To amend title 38, United States Code, to provide for a presumption of service-connection for male breast cancer occurring in certain veterans for purposes of determining eligibility for disability compensation under the laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs.
US-119-HR10882.aiSummary: The bill would make male breast cancer count as service-related for certain veterans when the Department of Veterans Affairs decides on disability pay. That means some veterans with male breast cancer could be more likely to qualify for VA disability compensation. It was introduced in the House and sent to the House Veterans' Affairs Committee.

US-119-HR10860.title: Stop Beijing’s Bots Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10860.description: To prohibit the Department of Defense from acquiring or using certain robotic systems from People's Republic of China, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10860.aiSummary: The bill would stop the Department of Defense from buying or using certain robotic systems tied to China. It would block new contracts for those systems within 1 year of enactment, bar use in sensitive military settings within 2 years, and limit lease funding, with some rules taking effect 1 year and 3 years after enactment. The Secretary of Defense could give short waivers in some cases and would have to tell Congress about them.

US-119-HR10783.title: Speak Your Truth Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10783.description: To provide for the payment of attorney's fees to a prevailing defendant in a civil action for defamation or libel.
US-119-HR10783.aiSummary: The bill would let a defendant who wins a federal defamation or libel case get reasonable lawyer fees and court costs paid by the person who sued. It applies to cases over a communication about sexual assault, harassment, or discrimination, if the statement was factual and made without malice. A judge could limit the award in special cases.

US-119-HR10761.title: Campus Accountability and Safety Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10761.description: To amend the Jeanne Clery Campus Safety Act to combat campus sexual assault, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10761.aiSummary: The bill would change the federal campus safety law for colleges that receive federal funds. It would require more public reporting on sexual assault and related cases, add clearer definitions, and put more campus safety and complaint information on a public website. It would also require each school to set up support steps for survivors, including trained violence specialists and victim-focused interview methods.

US-119-HR10684.title: DOE Bioenergy Program Reauthorization Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10684.description: To amend the Energy Policy Act of 2005 to support the research and development of bioenergy and renewable chemicals at the Department of Energy, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10684.aiSummary: The bill would update the Energy Policy Act of 2005 to support Department of Energy research, development, demonstration, and commercial use of bioenergy and renewable chemicals and materials. It would define terms like bioenergy, biomass, biomanufacturing, and biorefineries, and set up work on feedstocks, scale-up testing, data tools, sustainability, workforce training, and coordination with other agencies and groups. It would also require at least four small-scale process development or scale-up facilities and a grant program for new bioenergy ideas, plus demonstration projects for integrated biorefineries.

US-119-HR10563.title: Facial Recognition and Biometric Technology Moratorium Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10563.description: To prohibit biometric surveillance by the Federal Government without explicit statutory authorization and to withhold certain Federal public safety grants from State and local governments that engage in biometric surveillance.
US-119-HR10563.aiSummary: The bill would bar federal agencies and federal workers from using biometric surveillance, which means software that identifies people from face, voice, or other body traits, unless Congress gives clear permission in law. It would also block use of certain federal public safety grants for state or local governments that use biometric surveillance, starting with the first fiscal year after enactment. The measure would affect federal agencies, federal workers, and state and local governments that receive those grants.

US-119-HR9530.description: To require the Secretary of Transportation to issue regulations to prohibit certain cell phone voice communications on aircraft in scheduled passenger interstate or intrastate air transportation.

US-119-HR6021.title: Archie Cavanaugh Migratory Bird Treaty Clarification Act
US-119-HR6021.summary:
Archie Cavanaugh Migratory Bird Treaty Amendment Act

This bill states that nothing in the Migratory Bird Treaty Act of 1918 (MBTA) prohibits possessing, selling, bartering, purchasing, shipping, or transporting any authentic Alaska Native handicraft, clothing, or art on the basis that it contains a nonedible migratory bird part, so long as the bird was not taken in a wasteful or illegal manner. (The MBTA implements four international treaties that the United States entered into with Canada, Mexico, Japan, and Russia. The MBTA prohibits the taking of protected migratory bird species without prior authorization.)

The bill directs the Department of State to work with the Department of the Interior to enter into appropriate bilateral procedures with countries that are parties to the treaties under the MBTA to clarify the treatment of Alaska Native handicraft containing nonedible migratory bird parts from the species of migratory birds listed in those treaties. Further, Interior must modify any regulations implementing the MBTA to implement this bill.
US-119-HR6021.summarySource: Congressional Research Service summary (Introduced in House, 2025-11-12)

US-119-HR9772.title: Foreign Funding Transparency Act
US-119-HR9772.summary:
Foreign Funding Transparency Act

This bill requires certain organizations exempt from federal income tax to report to the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) information related to contributions received from foreign nationals.

The bill applies to tax-exempt organizations described in Section 501(c) of the Internal Revenue Code (e.g., charities, social welfare organizations, labor organizations, and business or civics leagues) with (1) gross receipts for the preceding tax year of $200,000 or more, or (2) assets (determined at the close of the preceding tax year) of $500,000 or more.

Such tax-exempt organizations that are required to file a Form 990 series information return with the IRS must report (1) the aggregate amount of contributions received during the tax year from foreign nationals, and (2) the portion of those contributions received from foreign nationals from China, Iran, Korea, or Russia.

Under the bill, a tax-exempt organization may rely on the representation of the donor as to nationality unless the organization knows or should know that such representation is false.

US-119-HR10101.title: Open Doors to Diplomacy Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Foreign Affairs.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10101.description: To amend the Foreign Service Act of 1980 to ensure that the Secretary of State improves outreach and recruitment efforts at nontraditional institutions of higher education, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10101.aiSummary: The bill would update the Foreign Service Act so the Secretary of State would improve outreach and recruiting at nontraditional colleges and schools, like community colleges and career and technical colleges. It would call for regular info sessions and prep help for people interested in Foreign Service jobs and other entry programs. It would also widen recruitment outreach to students enrolled full-time or at least half-time, including those at community colleges and similar schools.

US-119-HR9970.title: RESCUE Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR9970.description: To amend title XVIII of the Social Security Act to ensure appropriate payments for ambulance services under the Medicare program.
US-119-HR9970.aiSummary: The bill would change how Medicare pays for ambulance services, including both ground and air ambulance care. It would require the health secretary to review and update payment rates using newer cost and service data, with new rules starting in 2028 and yearly updates in some years after that. It would also require air ambulance providers to report certain data and would call for a stakeholder meeting by the end of 2028, with recommendations due by July 1, 2029.

Referred to the Subcommittee on Environment.

US-119-HR3194.description: To amend the Clean Air Act to prohibit State standards relating to the control of emissions from existing locomotives and engines used in locomotives, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR3194.aiSummary: The bill would change the Clean Air Act so states could not set their own rules for emissions from existing locomotives and the engines used in them. It would affect state governments and rail locomotives that are used in commerce, including common carrier railroad service for pay. The bill was introduced in the House and later sent to committee review.

US-119-HR9398.title: Historic Preservation and Land Conservation Certainty Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR9398.description: To provide an election to resolve certain open partnership controversies involving donations of conservation easements.
US-119-HR9398.aiSummary: The bill would let certain partnerships make a one-time election to settle open federal tax disputes tied to donations of conservation easements. If they use it, the partnership and related partners would give up the right to challenge certain settlement amounts, and the election would be available during a 180-day period after the law takes effect. It would apply to eligible contributions made on or before December 31, 2024, that still have unresolved tax matters.

US-119-HR9255.title: Timeshare Transparency Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR9255.description: To establish requirements with respect to the sale of timeshares to improve acquisition transparency, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR9255.aiSummary: The bill would set new rules for timeshare sales so buyers get a single document with all costs, ongoing fees, any fees the company can change, and ways to end ownership. It would also give buyers a 14-day right to cancel without penalty and a chance to review all papers on their own before signing. The Federal Trade Commission would enforce the rules, and they would apply to agreements made 90 days after the law takes effect.

US-119-HR9112.title: CREATOR Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR9112.description: To provide visuals artists the exclusive right to authorize the commercial exploitation, or public distribution in or affecting interstate commerce of a stylistic impersonation of that visual artist, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR9112.aiSummary: The bill would give visual artists a federal right to control the sale or public sharing of a style copy that imitates their work in commerce. It also sets rules for online services and AI tools, with notice-and-takedown steps and some uses like criticism, parody, research, news, and independent art left out. Courts could award damages and orders to stop violations, and the bill also limits some state claims that overlap with this new right.

US-119-HR9035.title: Ending Fossil Fuel Bailouts Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Natural Resources, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR9035.description: To amend title 11 of the United States Code to ensure oil, gas, and coal companies that are debtors in bankruptcy fulfill environmental reclamation obligations.
US-119-HR9035.aiSummary: This bill would change bankruptcy rules for oil, gas, and coal companies so cleanup and land restoration costs come first in payment order. It would also block these costs from being wiped out in bankruptcy, stop some fossil fuel assets from being abandoned, and let courts look back up to 10 years for certain transfers or debts tied to these companies. New federal fossil fuel leases would have to bar transfer if the leaseholder files for bankruptcy, and the changes would apply to bankruptcy cases started on or after the date the bill becomes law.

US-119-SJRES11.title: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management relating to "Protection of Marine Archaeological Resources".
US-119-SJRES11.summary:
This joint resolution rescinds a requirement for lessees and operators to submit an archaeological report with any oil and gas exploration or development plan they submit to the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM) for approval of activities proposed on the Outer Continental Shelf. (An archaeological report identifies material remains of human life or activities that are at least 50 years old and that are of archaeological interest.)

Specifically, the joint resolution nullifies BOEM's final rule titled Protection of Marine Archaeological Resources and published on September 3, 2024.

Nullifying this rule requires BOEM to reinstate regulations that were previously in effect and authorized BOEM to require an archaeological report only if a BOEM regional director has reason to believe that an archaeological resource may be present in the lease area.
